extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel involved in USPTO Part 42 post‑grant proceedings (petitioners, patent owners, patent practitioners, and their attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements governing petitions, motions, discovery, evidence, testimony, oral argument, decisions, settlement, and Director review in USPTO Part 42 post‑grant proceedings (e.g., IPR, PGR, CBM, derivation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency and limits of notices
rubrics_metrics.description: A failure to state a sufficient basis for relief may result in denial; a party is limited to filing motions consistent with the notice; ambiguities in the notice will be construed against the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correcting a notice, file promptly after learning the basis. A correction after the filing deadline will be entered only if it serves the interests of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of petitions and motions — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition or motion must be a separate paper and include (1) a statement of the precise relief requested; and (2) a full statement of the reasons for the relief requested, including a detailed explanation of the significance of the evidence including material facts, and the governing law, rules, and precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a rule in part 1 ordinarily governs the relief sought, the petition or motion must make any showings required under that rule in addition to the Part 42 showings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of material facts format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition or motion may include a statement of material fact; each material fact preferably shall be set forth as a separately numbered sentence with specific citations to the portions of the record that support the fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps the Board and opposing parties evaluate factual assertions; supports admission/denial mechanics in responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may order additional showings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may order additional showings or explanations as a condition for authorizing a motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 42.20(b) for authorization conditions; be prepared to provide supplemental detail when ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions/replies/sur-replies content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions, replies, and sur-replies must comply with the content requirements for motions and, if the paper being responded to contains a statement of material fact, must include a listing of facts that are admitted, denied, or cannot be admitted or denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material fact not specifically denied may be considered admitted. All arguments for relief must be made in the underlying motion; replies may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding opposition (or specified papers); sur-replies may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding reply and generally may not introduce new evidence except deposition transcripts of cross‑examination of any reply witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type‑volume and page limits — petitions and motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified word counts/page limits apply and include any statement of material facts to be admitted or denied; the word count/page limit excludes table of contents, table of authorities, mandatory notices under § 42.8, certificate of service or word count, and appendix exhibits or claim listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific limits: IPR petition 14,000 words; PGR petition 18,700 words; CBM petition 18,700 words; derivation petition 14,000 words; motions (excluding motions to amend) 15 pages; motions to amend 25 pages. Petitions to institute must comply but may be accompanied by a motion to waive word counts showing interests of justice and appending proposed overlength petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of word counts/page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to institute may be accompanied by a motion to waive word counts; the movant must show how waiver is in the interests of justice and append the proposed overlength petition; other motions to waive must be granted in advance of filing the overlength paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the motion is not granted, the overlength proposed petition may be expunged or returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word/page limits for patent owner responses and oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner preliminary response and patent owner response have the same word counts as the petition; page limits for oppositions are the same as those for corresponding motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word/page limits for replies and sur‑replies are separately specified (see other metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type‑volume limits for replies and sur‑replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies and sur‑replies have specified word counts/page limits that include any statement of facts in support of the reply and exclude certain items (TOC, TOA, listing of admitted/denied facts, certificate, appendix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifics: Replies to patent owner responses to petitions 5,600 words; replies to oppositions (excluding replies to oppositions to motions to amend) 5 pages; replies to oppositions to motions to amend 12 pages; sur‑replies to replies to patent owner responses 5,600 words. Papers subject to type‑volume limits must include a certification stating the number of words; parties may rely on their word‑processing system count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default filing times for oppositions and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Default times: an opposition is due one month after service of the motion; a reply is due one month after service of the opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party should seek relief promptly after the need for relief is identified. Delay in seeking relief may justify denial of relief sought. Motions must be filed according to a schedule set by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory initial disclosures and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to mandatory discovery requiring initial disclosures set forth in the Office Patent Trial Practice Guide; parties must submit any agreement reached on initial disclosures by no later than the filing of the patent owner preliminary response or the expiration of the time period for filing such a response; the initial disclosures shall be filed as exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon institution of a trial, parties may automatically take discovery of information identified in the initial disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery when no agreement — motion required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where parties fail to agree to the mandatory discovery, a party may seek such discovery by motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional discovery beyond the mandatory set requires a showing it is in the interests of justice (with statutory limits for certain proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of limited discovery — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A party is not entitled to discovery except as provided in the mandatory initial disclosures or as otherwise authorized in the subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery beyond mandatory initial disclosures is permitted only by agreement or Board authorization; post‑grant review further limits additional discovery to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by either party (§ 42.224).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization required to compel testimony or production
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking to compel testimony or production of documents or things must file a motion for authorization that describes the general relevance of the testimony, document, or thing and: for testimony, identify the witness by name or title; for a document or thing, describe the general nature of the document or thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When serving documents that are inconsistent with a party's position, the party must concurrently serve the documents containing the inconsistency. Privileged materials remain protected. This requirement extends to inventors, corporate officers, and persons involved in preparation or filing of the documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional discovery — standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may agree to additional discovery; if they fail to agree, a party may move for additional discovery and must show such additional discovery is in the interests of justice (with exceptions/limits for certain proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may specify conditions for additional discovery. Parties may obtain production during cross‑examination or authorized compelled testimony when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production of documents — format and location
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as ordered by the Board, a party producing documents shall either provide copies to the opposing party or make the documents available for inspection and copying at a reasonable time and location in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For production sought outside the U.S., the motion must identify the foreign country, explain why the party believes the witness or document can be compelled there (describe procedures and estimated time), and demonstrate reasonable efforts to secure agreement to produce/testify in the U.S., including offering to pay travel/production expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of testimony — affidavits vs. deposition transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncompelled direct testimony must be submitted as an affidavit. All other testimony, including testimony compelled under 35 U.S.C. 24, must be in the form of a deposition transcript. Video‑recorded testimony may be agreed to by parties but cannot be submitted without prior Board authorization; the Board may authorize live or video testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan filings and hearings consistent with the required form; obtain Board authorization before submitting non‑transcript testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and location for taking testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncompelled direct testimony may be taken at any time to support filings; otherwise testimony may only be taken during a testimony period set by the Board. During the testimony period, deposition testimony may be taken at any reasonable time and location within the U.S. before a disinterested official authorized to administer oaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncompelled deposition testimony outside the U.S. only by agreement of parties or Board order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition duration time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless stipulated or ordered otherwise, time limits apply to deposition testimony: for compelled deposition testimony — seven hours for direct examination, four hours for cross‑examination, and two hours for redirect examination; for uncompelled direct testimony, cross‑examination and subsequent stages have specified limits (seven hours, four hours, two hours respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may stipulate different timing or seek Board orders to modify these limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to taking deposition testimony, parties must agree on time and place; if they cannot, the party seeking testimony must initiate a conference with the Board. For direct deposition testimony, at least three business days prior to the conference (or if no conference, at least ten days prior to the deposition) the party seeking direct testimony must serve a list and copy of each document it intends to rely on and a list/proffer of access to anything other than a document it intends to rely on. The party must file a notice of deposition at least ten business days before a deposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross‑examination should ordinarily occur after any supplemental evidence and more than a week before the filing date for any paper in which the cross‑examination testimony is expected to be used. A party requesting cross of more than one witness may choose the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and content limits in deposition notices
rubrics_metrics.description: A direct deposition notice must list time/place, witness name/address, exhibits to be relied upon, and a general description of the scope and nature of testimony to be elicited. Cross‑examination is limited to the scope of the direct testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional parties wishing to take direct testimony at the same time must provide a counter‑notice listing exhibits and the scope/nature of testimony. Objections to defects in notice are waived unless the objecting party promptly seeks authorization to file a motion to quash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition procedures and transcript certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses must be sworn by an authorized officer. Q&A must be recorded in order. Exhibits used must be numbered per § 42.63(c) and served if not previously served. Objections noted on record. The witness shall read and sign the transcript (subject to waiver or refusal). The officer shall prepare a certified transcript with a certificate stating specified facts (sworn status, transcript authenticity, recorder identity, presence of opponents, place/date, officer's lack of disqualifying interest, and circumstances of refusal to sign if applicable). The proponent must provide copies to all parties and file testimony as an exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objections to deposition evidence must be made during the deposition or are waived; objections to qualifications, manner, evidence, or conduct must be noted on the record and preserved by timely motion to exclude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as ordered by the Board or agreed in writing, the proponent of the direct testimony shall bear all costs associated with the testimony, including reasonable costs of making the witness available for cross‑examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for transcript, travel, and other witness costs when planning to offer testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders and motions to seal
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may file a motion to seal containing a proposed protective order (e.g., default protective order in the Practice Guide). The motion must include a certification that the moving party has in good faith conferred or attempted to confer with other affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For good cause, the Board may issue orders forbidding disclosure, specifying terms/time/place, prescribing discovery methods, forbidding inquiry into certain matters, designating persons present, sealing depositions, protecting trade secrets, or requiring simultaneous sealed filings. If requesting default protective order entry, file confidential info under seal (need not serve).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling confidential information in petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner filing confidential information with a petition may file a motion to seal with a proposed protective order. If requesting the default protective order, the petitioner must file (but need not serve) the confidential information under seal. The patent owner may only access sealed information prior to institution by agreeing to the protective order terms or obtaining relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a non‑default protective order is requested, similar filing under seal is required and the patent owner may access only by agreeing to terms, agreeing to a jointly filed protective order, or obtaining entry of a protective order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: After denial of a petition to institute a trial or after final judgment in a trial, a party may file a motion to expunge confidential information from the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when confidential disclosures were filed but later should be removed following case disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privilege for patent practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications between a client and a USPTO patent practitioner or a foreign jurisdiction patent practitioner that are reasonably necessary and incident to the scope of the practitioner's authority shall receive the same protections of privilege under Federal law as if between a client and a U.S.‑authorized attorney, including limitations and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 'USPTO patent practitioner' is defined by § 11.7; 'foreign jurisdiction patent practitioner' is a person authorized to provide patent advice in a foreign jurisdiction with professional qualifications met. Practitioners receive same treatment as attorneys on issues affecting privilege or waiver, including communications with employees, assistants, and among practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of evidence — compliance required
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence not taken, sought, or filed in accordance with this subpart is not admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office records need not be certified for admissibility if they are records to which all parties have access. Specifications/drawings of U.S. patent applications or patents are admissible only to prove what they describe; if relying on data in a specification/drawing to prove the truth of the data, an affidavit by someone with first‑hand knowledge of how the data was generated must be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and modification of the Federal Rules of Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, the Federal Rules of Evidence apply to a proceeding. Portions relating to criminal proceedings, juries, and matters not relevant to Part 42 do not apply. Certain terminology in the Federal Rules is modified for Part 42 context (e.g., 'appellate court' means Federal Circuit; 'trial' or 'hearing' means time for taking testimony).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In determining foreign law, the Board may consider any relevant material or source, including testimony, whether or not admissible under the Federal Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of evidence and exhibit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence consists of affidavits, deposition transcripts, documents, and things. All evidence must be filed as an exhibit. When relying on documents in a language other than English, a translation and an affidavit attesting to its accuracy must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibit numbering: each party must uniquely number exhibits in ranges the Board specifies (petitioner 1001–1999; patent owner 2001–2999). Exhibit format requirements: each exhibit must have a label (with party name and unique number; trials and later filings also include names of parties and trial number), papers must have sequential page numbers, and the exhibit label affixed to the lower right corner of the first page without obscuring information. Maintain and serve a current exhibit list whenever evidence is served and file it when filing exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection timing and motion to exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: For deposition evidence, objections must be made during the deposition. For other evidence submitted during a preliminary proceeding, objections must be filed within ten business days of institution (and once trial instituted, objections must be filed within five business days of service of the evidence). Objections must identify grounds with sufficient particularity to allow correction via supplemental evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The party relying on evidence may respond with supplemental evidence within ten business days of service of the objection. A motion to exclude must be filed to preserve an objection; it must identify the objections in the record in order and explain them and may be filed without prior Board authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert testimony and technical tests/data
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony that does not disclose the underlying facts or data on which the opinion is based is entitled to little or no weight. Testimony on U.S. patent law or patent examination practice will not be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on a technical test or data, the party must provide an affidavit explaining why the test/data is used; how the test was performed and data generated; how the data is used to determine a value; how the test is regarded in the relevant art; and any other information necessary for the Board to evaluate the test and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument request and demonstrative exhibit timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may request oral argument on an issue raised in a paper at a time set by the Board; the request must be a separate paper specifying the issues to be argued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrative exhibits must be served at least seven business days before the oral argument and filed no later than the time of oral argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decisions, rehearing, and timing for requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may consider petitions/motions in any order and may grant, deny, dismiss, or enter any appropriate order. A request for rehearing may be filed without prior authorization; the burden to show a decision should be modified lies with the requester, who must specifically identify matters misapprehended or overlooked and where they were previously addressed. Timing: within 14 days of entry of a non‑final decision or decision to institute as to at least one ground; or within 30 days of entry of a final decision or a decision not to institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory decisions are not final for judicial review. For non‑panel decisions a party may request panel rehearing; a panel reviews for abuse of discretion. A decision whether to institute trial is final and nonappealable (but rehearing may be sought per the above).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of trial without final written decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may terminate a trial without rendering a final written decision where appropriate, including consolidation with another proceeding or pursuant to a joint request under 35 U.S.C. 317(a) or 327(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may jointly request termination; Board retains authority to terminate where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment scope, adverse judgment requests, recommendations, and estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: A judgment disposes of all issues that were, or by motion reasonably could have been, raised and decided. A party may request adverse judgment against itself at any time (examples: disclaimer, cancellation of all claims, concession of unpatentability or derivation, abandonment). A judgment may include recommendations for further action by an examiner or Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estoppel: Petitioners (except in derivation) or their privies are estopped in the Office from requesting or maintaining proceedings on a claim for which they obtained a final written decision on patentability in IPR, PGR, or CBM on any ground raised or that reasonably could have been raised, subject to exceptions (e.g., settlements under 35 U.S.C. 317 or 327). Patent applicants/owners are precluded from actions inconsistent with an adverse judgment (e.g., obtaining claims not patentably distinct from finally refused/canceled claims or amendments denied during trial), except where a different written description exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement filing and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may settle any issue but the Board is not a party to the settlement and may independently determine jurisdiction, patentability, or Office practice. Any agreement or understanding made in connection with termination must be in writing and a true copy filed with the Board before termination. A party may request that the settlement be treated as business confidential information and kept separate from the patent or application files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a timely request to keep settlement separate is filed, the settlement is only available to a government agency on written request to the Board or to any other person upon written request with the fee (§ 42.15(d)) and a showing of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director review — scope, timing, format, and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may review decisions on institution, final decisions, rehearing grants, or any other decision concluding a proceeding and may review interlocutory decisions involved in those decisions. The Director may initiate sua sponte review (absent exceptional circumstances, initiated within 21 days after expiration of the period for rehearing). A party may file one request for Director Review instead of a rehearing, subject to limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing: request must be filed within the time set in § 42.71(d) (14 or 30 days) unless an extension for good cause is granted. No response to a Director Review request is permitted absent Director authorization. Format/length must comply with § 42.6(a) and length limits for motions unless authorized. Absent Director authorization, a request may not introduce new evidence.
